routes.description: Mechanism-first skepticism argues that confidence in large evolutionary transitions outruns demonstrated chemical and genetic mechanisms, while Christian faith need not depend on resolving those scientific disputes.
routes.successCriteria: Show that at least one central evolutionary claim concerning purpose, human behavior, or body-plan innovation lacks a sufficiently demonstrated mechanism, making broad confidence premature without making faith depend on a specific creation chronology.

motionBridge.description: Unresolved mechanisms in major biological transitions make confident evolutionary explanations overreach.

centralBridges.description: Observed adaptive behavior does not by itself establish literal biological purpose or agency.
Large body-plan transitions require demonstrated genetic and chemical mechanisms rather than compressed narratives.
Evolutionary explanations of distinctively human behavior require identifiable biological evidence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Scientific consensus can preserve unsupported claims until their evidentiary basis is directly checked.
Christian fellowship and salvation do not require uniformity about evolutionary interpretation.

routes.description: Theistic evolutionary synthesis argues that experimentally observed cognition, agency, gene regulation, convergence, and inheritance enlarge evolutionary theory while remaining compatible with divine action and Christian faith.
routes.successCriteria: Show that modern evolutionary theory has empirically grounded mechanisms or research programs beyond blind mutation-selection, acknowledge its genuine limits, and establish that accepting this science does not conflict with central Christian commitments.

motionBridge.description: An empirically expanded and qualified evolutionary account can coexist coherently with Christian faith.

centralBridges.description: Experimental adaptive behavior supports cognition and agency as biologically relevant evolutionary phenomena.
Gene regulation, niche construction, convergence, and inheritance extend evolutionary explanation beyond a simplistic blind model.
Human uniqueness can be treated as divine creation without rejecting evolution elsewhere in life.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Scientific openness requires assessing heterodox proposals by experiments and data rather than labels.
Scriptural interpretation and core Christian confession permit disagreement about evolutionary history.

sections.title: Agency and cognition
sections.rationale: The claim that organisms possess experimentally tractable agency is the principal proposed expansion beyond a blind mutation-selection account.

sections.title: Human uniqueness
sections.rationale: Whether morality and other human capacities can be evolutionarily explained is a distinct central limit asserted by both speakers.

sections.title: Convergence and unknown laws
sections.rationale: Convergent structures test whether an unknown-law research program supplies explanation or merely redescribes unresolved biological regularities.

sections.title: Body plans and genome duplication
sections.rationale: The direct exchange over vertebrate body plans produces the debate's clearest mechanism challenge and its strongest evidentiary concession.

sections.title: Christian reconciliation
sections.rationale: The motion also requires assessing whether interpretive flexibility and core Christian commitments permit scientific disagreement without doctrinal conflict.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Bacterial sensing, interaction, avoidance, memory, and anticipatory metabolic change provide experimental grounds for treating agency and cognition as biologically real.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: Little bacteria have agency and they have purpose

moves.attributionBasis: The uninterrupted answer is clearly voiced by Garte and explicitly attributes agency, purpose, and cognition to bacteria.

response.rationale: This is the first selected constructive statement of the agency route and therefore has no earlier selected decisive target requiring component contact.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It directly establishes the adopted burden with several concrete behavioral capacities, though the mechanism remains undeveloped.

precisionFindings.rationale: The bacterial behaviors are clear, but agency, purpose, and cognition are grouped without fully distinguishing operational from philosophical meanings.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Experiments support sophisticated adaptive behavior, but the move advances purpose and cognition more strongly than the listed observations alone establish.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The observations form an intelligible route to richer biological capacities, with the behavior-to-agency bridge left partly implicit.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Specific experimental categories and a decade of work are invoked, but no individual study or operational criterion is developed here.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly advances the central bridge that modern evolutionary biology includes agency and cognition.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move does not yet represent or attack a live opposing alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: The selected span lists sensing, interaction, enemy avoidance, memory, and action without neurons as the empirical basis.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Calling single-cell behavior purposeful remains contestable because adaptive cellular conduct does not by itself establish purpose in the stronger sense asserted.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: to say that that that a cell has a purpose

moves.attributionBasis: The alternating dialogue and direct challenge to Garte make Tour's identity and the challenged proposition clear.

components.text: Bacteria display sensing, interaction, avoidance, memory, and anticipatory behavior.
Those observed behaviors warrant describing bacteria as possessing purpose and agency.

response.rationale: Tour directly questions the inference from cellular behavior to purpose, contacting the decisive interpretive component, but supplies no independent criterion that would resolve the dispute.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Contact is direct and decisive, but the reply mostly registers contestability rather than demonstrating a defeating defect.

precisionFindings.rationale: The challenge is recoverable and carefully limited, although it relies on the same unresolved ambiguity in the word purpose.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Tour frames the point as a challenge to be answered and does not claim that purpose has been disproved.

charity.alternative: Garte claims experimentally observed cellular behavior supports genuine biological purpose and agency.
charity.decisiveQualification: The claim concerns all life but is offered as an experimentally motivated biological proposal, not merely a theological assertion.

logicalCoherence.rationale: It correctly isolates the behavior-to-purpose inference, but does not provide a positive account separating apparent from genuine purpose.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The reply offers a legitimate conceptual objection but little evidence beyond anticipated materialist disagreement.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It attacks the decisive central bridge connecting adaptive cellular observations to biological agency.

representationalCharity.rationale: The stronger purpose claim is identified accurately, though Garte's experimental framing receives limited treatment.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour distinguishes readily accepted human purpose from the newer and more controversial attribution of purpose to a single cell.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Evolution does not explain the origin of life or fully define humanity because human moral and conscious qualities exceed available evolutionary principles.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: I don't think evolution applies everywhere in life

moves.attributionBasis: Garte explicitly qualifies his evolutionary-creationist position in a continuous first-person answer.

response.rationale: This selected span opens the human-uniqueness issue and does not answer an earlier selected move in the bounded inventory.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It sharply defines the scope of Garte's synthesis and its two major exclusions.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move expressly limits evolution at origins and humanity and clearly identifies the relevant human qualities.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The categorical claim that evolutionary principles cannot explain human qualities is not yet supported by the move's asserted evidence.

charity.alternative: Standard biologists explain human beings and their traits through evolutionary processes.
charity.decisiveQualification: Evolutionary accounts may concern predispositions and population effects rather than a single gene wholly determining morality.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The scoped synthesis is internally intelligible, but the inference from distinctive qualities to non-evolutionary creation remains materially compressed.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move asserts explanatory limits without yet supplying detailed comparative evidence against evolutionary accounts.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It centrally defines how the synthesis preserves human uniqueness while accepting evolution elsewhere.

representationalCharity.rationale: It acknowledges the standard evolutionary alternative but compresses its potentially multilevel explanations into a broad rejected category.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte expressly excludes origins and human definition from his general acceptance of evolution and cites human characteristics as the reason.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: An evolutionary account of prosocial human behavior requires identifiable heritable biological evidence rather than an adaptive story about cooperative groups reproducing more successfully.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: if that's the DNA that propagates Show me the DNA

moves.attributionBasis: Tour voices the group-selection account and then demands the DNA that allegedly propagates, with speaker turns clear from the exchange.

components.text: Human morality and related qualities are commonly given evolutionary explanations.
Those explanations fail because distinctively human qualities exceed evolutionary principles.

response.rationale: Tour supplies the evolutionary alternative and exposes its need for heritable evidence, but he does not establish Garte's stronger conclusion that human qualities are beyond evolutionary explanation.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The reply is issue-bearing and contacts the secondary evidentiary dispute, while leaving the target's decisive non-evolutionary conclusion unproved.

precisionFindings.rationale: The demand is clearly limited to a purported genetic evolutionary explanation of prosocial behavior.

calibrationFindings.rationale: For the genetic propagation account being discussed, requiring some identifiable heritable basis is proportionate.

charity.alternative: Cooperative dispositions could spread because cohesive groups protect members and reproduce more successfully.
charity.decisiveQualification: The proposed account can involve polygenic dispositions and population effects rather than one discrete kindness gene.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The demand for a heritable basis follows directly from the specific propagation account under discussion.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The methodological warrant is sound, though the move does not survey evidence for polygenic or cultural-gene coevolutionary accounts.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It advances the central pro demand for biological evidence behind explanations of human behavior.

representationalCharity.rationale: Tour states the cooperative-group account fairly, but his DNA demand risks suggesting an unduly simple single-gene model.

moves.evidenceBasis: The span reconstructs the survival-and-propagation account and asks for the genetic substrate that makes it evolutionary.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Invoking unspecified biological laws to explain independently arising complex features substitutes an unresolved placeholder for a causal evolutionary account.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: that appeal to an unspecific law substitutes for for a casual account

moves.attributionBasis: Tour reads Garte's stated conclusion and immediately identifies the missing causal account in his own explicit challenge.

response.rationale: The move introduces the selected convergence-mechanism challenge; the quoted book claim is not separately selected as an earlier transcript move.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It precisely identifies the causal burden that the ensuing convergence explanation must discharge.

precisionFindings.rationale: The objection clearly targets unspecified laws as insufficient causal explanation for the listed convergent features.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Tour argues that the stated unknown-law appeal is presently unusable, not that no such laws could exist.

charity.alternative: Repeated convergence indicates unknown structural laws constrain evolutionary outcomes.
charity.decisiveQualification: The proposal openly labels the laws unknown and presents them as a research clue rather than a completed mechanism.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between identifying a regularity and supplying its causal mechanism is clear and directly applicable.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The quoted claim supports the criticism, though the move does not yet consider whether explanatory constraint can precede a known mechanism.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the central pro requirement for causal mechanisms behind major evolutionary claims.

representationalCharity.rationale: The unknown-law claim is quoted accurately, but its explicitly exploratory status is somewhat underweighted.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour quotes the appeal to unknown biological laws and explains why it does not yet provide a usable causal pathway.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Repeated independent convergence on complex structures makes wholly unconstrained chance implausible and supplies evidence for structural constraints worth investigating even before their laws are known.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: there must be some laws and these are often called structuralism

moves.attributionBasis: Garte's continuous answer names Gould, Conway Morris, convergent eyes and wings, and the proposed structuralist inference.

components.text: The proposed biological laws are unspecified and therefore lack a completed mechanism.
An unspecified law cannot presently function as a full causal account.

response.rationale: Garte answers why unknown laws are inferred by presenting convergence as evidence of constraint, but concedes that the laws remain unknown and does not supply the requested causal account.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The decisive epistemic basis for positing constraints is directly addressed, although the causal-mechanism demand remains unresolved.

precisionFindings.rationale: Convergence and structural laws are clear, but the scope of what mutation and selection allegedly cannot explain is broader than demonstrated.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Independent convergence supports constraints, but the claim that matching complex eyes has almost zero chance and cannot arise under selection is insufficiently warranted.

charity.alternative: Unknown laws merely rename the absence of a causal evolutionary pathway.
charity.decisiveQualification: The criticism concerns present causal adequacy, not whether convergence is a legitimate phenomenon requiring research.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference from repeated convergence to constrained outcomes is intelligible, but it does not itself identify the source of constraint.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Eyes and wings are concrete examples, yet probability claims and rival explanations such as functional selection are not seriously compared.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The reply centrally supports an expanded evolutionary research program while directly engaging the mechanism objection.

representationalCharity.rationale: Garte recognizes that Tour wants a causal account and candidly concedes that the proposed laws remain unknown.

moves.evidenceBasis: The span cites independent octopus and human eyes, multiple origins of wings, and Conway Morris's convergence research.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Whole-genome duplication does not by itself explain the chemical and genetic steps required to transform an invertebrate body plan into a vertebrate one.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: how much chemistry has to take place to have a body plan change

moves.attributionBasis: Tour quotes the genome-duplication account and explicitly challenges the unexplained transition to a vertebrate body plan.

response.rationale: This is the selected constructive formulation of the body-plan mechanism burden; the book passage it challenges is embedded rather than separately scored.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It isolates the exact large-scale transition and the missing mechanistic steps with exceptional clarity.

precisionFindings.rationale: The move precisely limits its criticism to the explanatory leap from duplication to vertebrate anatomy.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Tour argues that the supplied account is insufficient and asks for steps, without claiming that the transition is impossible.

charity.alternative: Genome duplication creates redundant material that can mutate and facilitate new vertebrate structures.
charity.decisiveQualification: The alternative proposes an enabling genomic event, not necessarily a complete one-sentence chemical mechanism.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The enabling-event versus complete-mechanism distinction is coherent and exposes a material missing bridge.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The quoted account makes the compression concrete, though Tour supplies a demand for evidence rather than independent contrary data here.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly advances the central mechanism-first burden concerning large body-plan transitions.

representationalCharity.rationale: The duplication account is represented accurately, with only minor compression of its possible enabling rather than sufficient role.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour quotes the asserted duplication and rapid anatomical innovation, then asks for the chemistry underlying the invertebrate-to-vertebrate transition.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: A literature check failed to find molecular evidence that whole-genome duplication causes the large mutation event needed for the asserted vertebrate transition, so the challenged account should be withdrawn.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: it's never been shown that a whole genome duplication results

moves.attributionBasis: Garte recounts his search, reports the consistent paper findings, and expressly tells Tour that the objection is correct.

components.text: Whole-genome duplication is asserted as enabling large-scale mutation and vertebrate innovation.
The asserted transition lacks demonstrated molecular steps from duplication to body-plan change.

response.rationale: Garte contacts both components, reports that the searched literature states the event has not been shown, and explicitly concludes that Tour is right and the original account is not true.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: The answer is unusually complete because it verifies the decisive objection against multiple papers and expressly concedes its consequence.

precisionFindings.rationale: The concession clearly concerns large-scale mutation after whole-genome duplication and does not deny every evolutionary role for duplication.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The literature search strongly supports withdrawing the specific assertion, although ten Google Scholar papers do not justify every broader formulation that it is unreal.

charity.alternative: Tour argues that duplication does not supply the mechanistic steps for vertebrate body-plan innovation.
charity.decisiveQualification: Tour challenges explanatory sufficiency and demonstrated steps, not the occurrence of genome duplication itself.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The reported search directly tests the disputed prediction and the concession follows cleanly from the negative finding.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Multiple papers reportedly agreed that the large mutation event had not been shown, though the search method and papers are not individually documented.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move decisively bears on the central mechanism bridge by validating the specific body-plan objection.

representationalCharity.rationale: Garte identifies Tour's precise objection, investigates it on its own terms, and concedes the result without weakening it.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte describes checking ten papers, finding no molecular evidence for the postulated large mutation event, and withdrawing his prior assumption.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Disputed creation interpretations are secondary to the Christian confession of Jesus as risen Lord, and scriptural seriousness permits more than one reading of cosmological language.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: There's different ways of interpreting that same verse

moves.attributionBasis: Tour clearly contrasts salvation essentials with creation disputes and supplies Psalm 104 as an example of interpretive flexibility.

response.rationale: The selected move constructively establishes Tour's reconciliation position and does not answer an earlier selected move in this section.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It gives both a doctrinal criterion and a concrete interpretive example, though it does not directly establish evolutionary mechanisms.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between salvation essentials, secondary disputes, and alternative verse readings is stated clearly.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The theological conclusion is proportionate to the stated confessional criterion and the example of nonliteral cosmological interpretation.

charity.alternative: A literal creation interpretation may be treated as essential to scriptural fidelity or salvation.
charity.decisiveQualification: Tour does not devalue scripture; he argues that serious interpretation can yield different readings.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between core salvation doctrine and secondary interpretive disagreements is explicit and consistently applied.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Tour quotes the operative Christian confession and gives a scriptural interpretive analogue, though denominational alternatives are not explored.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move advances the subsidiary faith bridge rather than resolving the motion's scientific mechanism dispute.

representationalCharity.rationale: Tour expressly preserves scriptural seriousness while rejecting the claim that one creation reading determines salvation.

moves.evidenceBasis: The span invokes confession of the risen Jesus and Psalm 104 to distinguish core faith from disputable scientific interpretation.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Christian faith and scientific practice are compatible, so neither atheist exclusion of faith nor religious rejection of science should prevent Christians from pursuing science.

sourceSpan.evidenceCue: science and Christian faith are at odds with each other

moves.attributionBasis: Garte delivers the uninterrupted closing statement of his books' purpose and directly rejects conflict from both academia and churches.

response.rationale: This is Garte's closing constructive statement of the motion-level reconciliation claim, not a reply to an earlier selected opposing move.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It directly states and applies the reconciliation conclusion, but its historical support is overstated.

precisionFindings.rationale: Compatibility is clear, but perfect harmony and the universal historical claims expand the scope without necessary qualification.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The compatibility conclusion is defensible, but perfect harmony and the claim of no early atheist scientists exceed the supplied warrant.

charity.alternative: Atheist academics may teach that faith conflicts with science, while some churches teach that science must be rejected.
charity.decisiveQualification: The opposing groups are described only at their radical edges and do not represent every atheist academic or conservative church.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The compatibility conclusion follows from the possibility of faithful scientific practice, but historical pedigree is not sufficient to prove perfect harmony.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move relies heavily on broad historical assertions and unspecified prevalence rather than representative evidence.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the complete motion-level conclusion that Christian faith can be reconciled with scientific evolutionary inquiry.

representationalCharity.rationale: Both conflict positions are recognized, but they are represented through their most radical formulations.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte identifies conflict teaching in both academia and churches, asserts compatibility, and applies it to Christian students considering scientific careers.
